title: arXiv AI trending — Monday, 26 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; the ordering is inferred from observed paper-list upvotes and independent curation. Citation evidence is limited for these recent papers, and no citation totals are reported.

sections.title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods
sections.abstract: RSIHub is an open framework for composing and comparing agent-evolution methods with shared execution, evaluation, recovery, and lineage services.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper presents a composable framework that instantiates four agent-evolution methods without changing its core, and reports gains up to 13.5 percentage points while showing that method rankings and held-out transfer vary by setting.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that the evidence depends on trusted framework and host services, valid evaluators, and tested workloads; the experiments cover fixed recipes, not adaptive recipe revision by an outer agent.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 24 upvotes in the 26 October daily paper list; #3 overall in that list.

sections.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
sections.abstract: RynnUnify combines embodied understanding, interleaved video-language planning, and robot-action extensions in a 16B model, with evaluations spanning visual planning and simulated and real-robot tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a unified embodied model and extensions for planning and robot control; they report a 9.75-point improvement over Cosmos 3 Nano on Rynn-VP, gains on Rynn-GEU, and 46.7% average success across three real-robot tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report that generated videos can distort fine geometry and call for broader validation of physical execution across tasks and environments; the real-robot result covers three tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 17 upvotes in the 26 October daily paper list (#5 overall), plus #5 in ArXiv TLDR's weekly curated list updated 26 October.

sections.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
sections.abstract: TWIG represents neural-network weights as paths of shared discrete decisions, unifying compression edits and enabling shift-and-add implementations for suitable hardware.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper proposes TWIG as a shared representation for pruning, quantization, factorization, codebooks, and weight sharing; on LLaMA-3-8B it reports 9–15% fewer adders than GPTQ at equal layer error on typical matrices at 3- and 4-bit settings, with up to 55% fewer on outlier-heavy matrices.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe these as first measurements on selected models and layers; adder counts omit adder width and fixed-point truncation effects, making them a first-order circuit-size proxy rather than measured area. Direct training in TWIG remains future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 4 upvotes in the 26 October daily paper list (#7 overall).

sections.title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation
sections.abstract: DraMaze combines trope-guided evolutionary search with a backward narrative-dependency memory tree and a bilingual benchmark for long microdrama scripts.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that DraMaze reduces causal-pattern repetition by 32.1% and reaches a Logic score of 82.5 on 60-episode scripts, outperforming the best baseline by 8.5 points across their tested setup.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence concerns bilingual microdrama generation and three backbone LLMs; it does not establish improvement in other long-form writing domains or human audience outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 3 upvotes in the 26 October daily paper list (#8 overall).

sections.title: Easy-3Dfy: Object-Level Geometric Composition for Single-Image 3D Scene Construction
sections.abstract: Easy-3Dfy separates object generation from scene-layout estimation and aligns generated object meshes with partial scene point maps to construct 3D scenes from one image.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper proposes a modular geometric-composition workflow and reports better results than SAM-3Dfy across multiple geometric metrics on Scene-Maker and 3D-FUTURE200.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evaluation is on those two benchmarks and relies on specialized object generators; the abstract does not establish transfer to other scene distributions or capture conditions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 3 upvotes in the 26 October daily paper list (#10 overall).

sections.title: DirCast: Live Esports Directing and Commentary with a Single Streaming Video-Language Model
sections.abstract: DirCast uses one streaming video-language model to select among player-camera feeds and generate commentary for live esports broadcasts from past frames.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors build a 27-match Dota 2 multi-camera dataset and report better directing than rule-based and zero-shot baselines, with commentary preferred in 29.2% of comparisons against GPT-4o under Proact-VL.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is specific to 27 professional Dota 2 matches and the reported comparison protocol; cross-game or real broadcast deployment is not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 3 upvotes in the 26 October daily paper list (#13 overall).

sections.title: Tool-Calling LLM Agents Under Realistic MCP Faults: Scale Does Not Purchase Fault Tolerance
sections.abstract: MCP-Injector tests tool-calling agents under failures calibrated from public MCP ecosystem incidents and finds severe task degradation under its fault profile, with no measured resilience gain from the larger of two tested backbones.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce protocol-aware MCP fault injection calibrated from 57,240 issue and pull-request threads and report a 60% task-completion-score drop in a 1,350-cell evaluation.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported scale comparison is between two GPT-OSS backbones (20B and 120B), three agent stacks, and a permanent-heavy stress profile; it does not quantify failure rates for every deployed MCP system.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: ArXiv TLDR selected it as #1 in its weekly AI-paper list updated 26 October.

sections.title: The Butterfly Defects: Tracing Cooperation in LLM Agent Networks
sections.abstract: Experiments using the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma show that cooperation among open-weight LLM agents changes with network composition, position, and small linguistic framing changes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports that cooperation is not stable across homogeneous and mixed populations, and that changing action-label order or adding uncertainty cues can alter behavior and affect agents several network hops away.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence comes from Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma interactions with open-weight models; it should not be read as a general measurement of cooperation in deployed multi-agent systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: ArXiv TLDR selected it as #2 in its weekly AI-paper list updated 26 October.

sections.title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
sections.abstract: The study measures both inference energy and execution energy for LLM-generated code optimizations, finding that faster code is often more energy-intensive than human reference code in its benchmark setting.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across 11 open-source models and 1,000 EffiBench problems, the paper reports that 42 of 44 tested configurations used more execution energy per problem than canonical human solutions; it also identifies output-token limits and model architecture as energy levers.
sections.unique_caveat: These measurements concern the evaluated open models, configurations, benchmark, and hardware setup; they do not imply the same energy trade-off for all code-generation workloads or deployment systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: ArXiv TLDR selected it as #4 in its weekly AI-paper list updated 26 October.

sections.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
sections.abstract: RobustRLlib unifies 17 robust online, offline, and safe reinforcement-learning algorithms and evaluates them across diverse shift and perturbation settings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a common library and benchmark covering 17 algorithms and 273 perturbation configurations, with the aim of exposing where existing robust-RL methods work and where they fail.
sections.unique_caveat: The empirical capability map is bounded by the selected algorithms, tasks, and perturbations; performance in the suite does not guarantee robustness in an untested real deployment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: ArXiv TLDR selected it as #10 in its weekly AI-paper list updated 26 October.
